title: Hear God's Voice Today: The 3 Bible Tests
hook: Before you call it 'God,' run it through these 3 tests.
script: Before you call it 'God,' run it through these 3 tests. Don't let anxiety wear God's name tag. First, the Scripture test: does this line up with the clear voice He's already given? 'My sheep hear my voice' (John 10:27), and all Scripture equips us (2 Tim 3:16). Second, the wisdom test: James 3:17 says godly wisdom is pure, peaceable, gentle, open to reason, full of mercy. Panic, pride, and secrecy are red flags. Third, the community and peace test: seek counsel (Proverbs 11:14) and let Christ's peace be the umpire (Colossians 3:15). If counsel confirms and peace remains, take the next small obedient step.

title: Fear or Father? How to Discern Fast
hook: If God feels silent right now, watch this.
script: If God feels silent right now, watch this. Silence can push us into impulsive choices, but God isn’t confusing you. Run the impression through three filters. Bible: does it agree with Scripture’s heart and commands? Wisdom: James 3:17—pure, peaceable, gentle, reasonable. Community and peace: ask trusted believers, then notice if Christ’s peace settles in. Quick example: 'Apologize to your friend.' Scripture affirms reconciliation. It’s humble and peaceable. Your mentor would nod. Peace grows—obey. Counterexample: 'Quit everything today or God will leave you.' That’s fear-based, manipulative, isolating, and not biblical. Breathe, pray Psalm 23, wait for the Shepherd’s steady peace, then move one step.

title: 60-Second Practice to Hear God
script: Grab 60 seconds with me. You may be overthinking this. Write the impression on your heart. Now filter it fast. Scripture: does the Bible support it? Wisdom: does it look like James 3:17—pure, peaceable, gentle, open to reason? Community and peace: would godly counsel agree, and does Christ’s peace rule as you pray? If it passes, choose one simple step today. If not, pause without shame and ask God for clarity. Dry season? It doesn’t mean God is gone. He’s steadying you. Journal what you tried, what passed, and any small confirmations. Watch patterns form. That’s how sheep learn their Shepherd.
